attempts.summary: Configured a 3-member MariaDB Galera cluster across node1/node2/node3 (CentOS Stream 10, mariadb-server-galera 10.11.18). Installed packages, opened firewalld ports (3306,4444,4567/tcp+udp,4568) with SELinux mysqld_port_t already covering them, wrote /etc/my.cnf.d/galera.cnf on each node with wsrep_cluster_address=gcomm://node1,node2,node3, bootstrapped node1 via galera_new_cluster, then joined node2 and node3. Verified multi-master write propagation: inserts from each node's local mysqld appeared on all others. Demonstrated availability during a member outage (stopped node2, cluster stayed Primary at size 2, writes from node1/node3 succeeded) and automatic resynchronization (started node2, it rejoined via IST to cluster size 3, state Synced, and had all rows including those written during its downtime). Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured boot_id baseline and health on all three nodes, sequentially rebooted each one at a time via systemctl reboot, confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and verified MariaDB auto-started (enabled unit) and cluster returned to full Primary/size-3/Synced health with intact data after each restart, waiting for full quorum before proceeding to the next node. Final cross-node write/read check post-restart confirms full functionality. Database credentials were generated on node1 via openssl and distributed to node2/node3 over cluster SSH without ever appearing in command text or this report.
